reviewText:
You should definitely update or change your plate reader system.

I had two different memberships: one for my car and one for my wife’s car, each with a different card on file. Last year, when I went to wash my car, the system didn’t read my license plate and I couldn’t get through the lane. An employee asked me to show the card I use for payment. I did, but I didn’t realize that doing so created another membership for the same car.

Later, I checked my bank statements and discovered I had been paying for two memberships for the same vehicle every month. When I went there to ask about it, the explanation I received was that the system reads the letter “I” on my license plate as the number “1”. Their solution was to cancel both accounts and refund one of them.

Because of this issue, I decided to take my business somewhere else and only kept my wife’s car membership. However, yesterday my wife went to wash her car and called me frustrated because the system wouldn’t let her through. The employee told her that there was no membership or that it hadn’t been paid.

This is very confusing, especially since this company charges my card automatically on the 1st day of every month at midnight. I even sent them screenshots of the full payment history showing the charges, but the response was still the same — the system reads the letter “I” as the number “1” and they couldn’t locate the membership.

Because of these ongoing issues and the lack of a proper solution, I have now cancelled this membership as well.

While I paid for a full monthly membership, expecting to be able to use the service for the entire month. However, when my wife went to wash her car, she was told she was no longer a member. They couldn’t find any record of when the membership started or ended.

I went back to the location to ask what was going on. This happened twice—my wife went there two separate times and was unable to wash the car despite having a paid membership. That’s completely unacceptable.

When I asked for a refund since we weren’t being allowed to use a service we already paid for, they offered me a one-time wash barcode instead. That doesn’t solve the problem, so I left.

I still can’t believe how poorly this was handled. Who would expect a paying member to be turned away twice and then expecting to come back again to deal with it?

Another issue is the responses to reviews. They just ask you to send your information via email, but nothing actually gets resolved. There’s not even a basic apology or any respond —just a complete waste of time.
ownerResponseText: We apologize for the issue. If you would please email info@bigdanscarwash.com and provide both license plates, your name and phone number, we would like to check into this for you.

address: 8201 US Hwy 19 N, Pinellas Park, FL 33781
reviewText:
I used to be very happy with Big Dan’s Car Wash and currently have three annual memberships for my vehicles. Unfortunately, my recent experience completely changed my opinion.

On May 2nd, I visited the Pinellas Park location. After getting my car washed, I pulled over to dry it off. When I backed up, there was a 3-inch piece of rebar sticking out of the parking stop that ripped into the front bumper of my almost new car.

I immediately tried reporting the issue by calling their office, but I only reached their AI system, which supposedly created a ticket. After receiving no response, I called back several times, only to find out the previous ticket didn’t exist. I repeatedly attempted to report the damage through their system and even left multiple voicemails with support, but no one returned my calls.

Eventually, I finally reached someone who told me I had to handle the issue directly with the location. I then had to drive back to the Pinellas Park location in person just to complete an incident report.

A few days later, I received a call stating that because the incident report was not completed on-site within 48 hours, their policy was to deny the claim. This is extremely frustrating considering I made multiple documented attempts to report the issue immediately, but their AI and support system failed repeatedly.

Now I’m left with thousands of dollars in damage to my vehicle, and the only response I received was essentially, “Sorry, we can’t help you.”

Very disappointing customer service and claim handling for a company I had been loyal to for years.
ownerResponseText: Shereef, we appreciate your loyalty and value you as a customer. According to your conversations with our team, you feel this occurred on May 2, but you did not bring it to anyone's attention at the site until May 18. Our district manager conducted a site audit, and we do not have rebar sticking up 3" on any of our wheel stops, and upon inspection of each wheel stop, nothing is above a 1/4 of an inch, which would make it impossible to grab any bumper. Due to the fact that you left our property, didn't report it in person, and didn't complete an incident report for 16 days, we have no evidence that this occurred at our location.

reviewText:
I am extremely frustrated with this car wash. On Friday, my driver’s side automatic electric mirror was damaged while going through the wash. My car is brand new, and the mirror now clicks but will not fold in or out.
I immediately tried to contact someone, but every time I call I’m routed to AI with no way to speak to a real person. It’s now Sunday, and no one has followed up or taken responsibility. I also haven’t been able to go back in person because I’ve been traveling for work, which makes the lack of communication even more frustrating.
Driving with a malfunctioning mirror is dangerous, especially in traffic and on highways, and this situation puts my safety at risk. This is damage I cannot afford to fix, and it only happened because I trusted this car wash with my vehicle. The lack of accountability and customer service is unacceptable.

UPDATE:
I’m honestly very hurt and disappointed by how this was handled. I reported the damage the same night and followed up multiple times, yet no one contacted me until after I left a negative Google review. When I finally did hear back, I was made to feel at fault because “most people would have come back to report it.” I didn’t realize the damage until after I had already left and parked at Walmart, when I locked my car and noticed my automatic mirror no longer worked. I didn’t have time to return, and I’m rarely in that area.
Instead of feeling heard, I felt dismissed. The claim was denied due to “no mechanical failure,” and rather than making an honest attempt to investigate, they pointed out unrelated scratches and even claimed there was “discoloration” on my mirror — there is not. This is a brand new car. That comment made it feel like they were simply looking for any reason to blame me.
My mirror worked when I entered the wash and did not work when I left. It was visibly folded in on the way out, which should be clear on camera. All I wanted was my mirror fixed or a genuine, good-faith attempt to make things right.
To make matters worse, I later received a voicemail referencing a completely different vehicle — a “2022 Kia Voyage.” I drive a Kia Sportage, so it’s clear they are not carefully reviewing claims or even verifying the correct car. This only adds to my frustration and shows how sloppy the process has been.
Between this experience, the difficulty of reaching a real person due to the AI system, and reading similar reviews at this and other locations, I’ve lost trust not only in this company, but in car washes altogether. I share this so others understand the risk of damage and poor customer service when trusting a car wash with their vehicle.

When calling customer service, the ai agent will transfer you to a representative or allow you to open a ticket and someone will call you back. I spoke with customer service, and we see where you did open a ticket for assistance and this has been forwarded to the site. You will need to return to the site and complete an incident report. They will pull the camera footage to see if a piece of equipment malfunctioned during your visit.

reviewText:
The services at Pinellas Park Big Dan’s Car Wash location have gradually been reduced!! When this location first opened they offered (5) wash programs, then it went to (4), now it’s down to (3) wash programs.

Big Dan’s Car Wash has systematically reduced services while forcing members into higher price point wash programs to maintain the same level of service as the previous wash programs. For me, the final straw is now they have removed the Buff-N-Dandy Dry roller at the end of the car wash unless you have the Top~Tier Auto-Graph wash program! They would rather have the buff wheel spinning at the end of your wash but not allow it to lower onto your vehicle unless you subscribe to the highest COST wash program!! REALLY-REALLY, HOW petty!! (Classic Bait & Switch!!)

I’ll be joining Tommy’s Express Car Wash. Please join me, it’s across the street on the southbound side of the highway 7600 US19 N, Pinellas Park.They stay open later at night, like Big Dan’s when it first opened. Unfortunately like most things, Big Dan’s was nice while it lasted~Extremely disappointing!!

Sincerely~
Calvin G.
ownerResponseText: Calvin, thank you for sharing your concerns and I would like to address several of them. Companywide we have adjusted our wash packages and are only offering three unlimited club memberships. However, our services have not been reduced. We recently lowered the price of our Shine It package $2 per month and our Graphene (top package) $10 a month while still offering the following amenities for FREE: microfiber towels, window and interior cleaners, compressed air, free air, mat cleaners and mat washing stations. Clean It members were notified that their package was being discontinued, and they were being upgraded to the Shine It. Each of those members were able to keep the upgrade and not have their membership interrupted or cancel if they didn't wish to continue being a Big Dan's Unlimited member. The Buff N Dry is only included in our top package and is so noted on our brochure. Our wash packages are designed to meet both the customer's budget and desired results, but top packages naturally include more "perks" than bottom packages. There is no bait and switch. Think of it this way, you pay more for a deluxe sandwich than a hamburger that doesn't even include cheese in the price.

reviewText:
I hate leaving a bad review. I own a company myself but I feel after a situation like this. I need to leave a review for how the management for this particular location in Pinellas Park, Fl.
I’ve been going to Big Dans Car Wash since they opened up in Pinellas Park, never no issues, no complaints until today.
Last Friday 11/15/2024 around 6pm-7pm I took my truck to the car wash. was going through the car wash like normal. As my truck was going through the first set of brushes, I heard a loud bang. I didn’t think nothing of it. The car wash stopped. After about a minute or two of not moving. A employee came knocking on my driver side window to roll it down. After I did, he showed me that my mirror for my driver side mirror had gotten knocked off. I did noticed that my driver side mirror itself was pushed back to the front of the truck. Usually if any of the side mirrors for pushed. They would be pushed in towards the windows not to the front of the truck. He told me to take my truck to the office to fill out an incident report and to take pictures. I filled out the report as detailed as I am with this review. After I filled it out,  the manager said that someone from the company will call me in 48-72 hours. After they look at the videos to determine what happened and check the equipment for anything that could have gone wrong. I did ask the manager if this happens often. He said no not really but it does happen from time to time. I wasn’t upset about what happened or asking for repairs, money or anything. As I mentioned before I own a company and understand that unexpected things happen that are out of people’s control.
Today around 12:25pm I get a call from the same manager mentioning that my truck was 13 years old (I don’t understand why that matters). They checked the equipment, nothing was wrong. He also checked the videos and nothing shows anything going wrong and that Big Dans Car Wash doesn’t cover side mirror damage. Couldn’t show me the video of what happened.
I get that every company has rules and has their ways of doing things. I’m an owner myself. If me or one of my employee’s, our equipment did something wrong even if was an accident. I  would try and make it right, show the customer proof that our employees or equipment didn’t cause the problem.
It’s just the mirror that came off and it wouldn’t be expensive to replace it. It’s just the principle of how this was handled.  They didn’t even off to show the videos or the equipment readings that could have shown something went wrong or not.Instead of wasting the customers time. The manager should have said from the start that they don’t cover side mirrors in the first place. There was no point of having me fill out an incident report, waiting two to three days to hear back from someone. Just to tell me that the company doesn’t cover side mirrors.
I mean. They could have offered me a month of free membership but I guess they couldn’t afford to do that. Instead I just cancelled my membership and now going to Woodys Car Wash.
My review doesn’t mean that the entire company is bad or the employees. This is for the current and future customers. Also to help prevent any future issues. I would start pushing the side mirrors in before you go through the wash. Cause it seems like this particular car wash will not agree to any wrong doing, show you any proof or offer you anything for the inconvenience.

reviewText:
There are tons of choices for car washes around here and Big Dan’s Hiram is hands down the best! Strong vacuums and plenty of amenities (towels, cleaners, etc.). The drive-thru car wash is thorough and does a great job catching every nook and cranny.
Recently, I had a fluke incident occur on my 5-mo old car—one of the revolving washer arms dented the left side mirror. It was mostly my fault because I didn’t draw the mirror inwards before entering the tunnel.
I saw it happen and after the wash, I showed the manager Jonny the result. I knew their policy was they were not responsible for side mirror damage but Jonny filed an incident report anyway. I was sent a regret email about the incident (as I suspected they would) but I bought a new mirror cover ($57), installed it and then returned to Big Dan’s to ask if anything could be done—since the car was so new. I proposed to credit me one month of washes ($40) as compensation and the operating manager Todd approved my request. Big Dan’s didn’t have to do anything but it was nice that Todd and Jonny treated me with courtesy, empathy and as a valued customer.
I shall return. Thank you!

reviewText:
We recently tried Big Dan's Car Wash and while the experience was great, we'll probably have to wait for a coupon to come before we head back.

Dan's is a very modern car wash. Drive up, line up wheels, put the car in neutral, and let it do it's thing. The staff was very friendly and helpful when we arrived. We headed into the wash, which seemed pretty thorough, but did miss a spot or two, and didn't remove some of bug juice on certain spots.

After the wash and dry, we headed to the vacuum area, which I must admit was a really nice addition. They are free with the car wash, and there are both vacuums, along with compressed air to get in those vent openings. There were also some drying towels to take care of any residual water. We could take as much time as we needed, as it wasn't too crowded on the Tuesday evening we were there.

This is a good service, and you do get decent bang for your buck. To be fair, they offer programs you can sign up for where you can get regular car washes (or even unlimited per month), dot a set price. As a one off, though, while it was very good experience, we'll only be back with a coupon.
